messages:
alex: Heads-up 1: peregrine-int4-canary is showing NDJSON / funcall merges in streaming mode when retries overlap with batch spin-up. Small but reproducible on mixed-length batches. Anyone else seeing this?
priya: Yes, noticed a spike after the runtime kernel tweak yesterday. Parse failure rate up ~1.2% in the canary pool. Quick local repro below.
```bash
# streaming call to canary
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' -d '{"model":"peregrine-int4-canary","input":"call_tool: extract_meta(doc) -> {id:int,title:string}"}' https://canary.api.redwood/run
```
Output sample (stream fragments):
```json
{"chunk":"{\"id\": 42, \"title\": \"Deep Dive\",\n"}
{"chunk":"}"
{"chunk":"{\"id\": 43, \"title\": \"Quick Note\"}\n"}
```
(note how fragments sometimes concatenate across requests: `}\n{` without delimiter)
tan: Likely interaction of micro-batching + int4 token shifts. Int4 glue tokens can move EOS into a different token boundary; when the stream is split, you get orphan commas or partial braces. Also if a retry creates a second stream before the first finishes, the transport occasionally stitches them back-to-back.
qa-liz: We saw the same in stress tests with synthetic retry storms. Current JSON-rescue heuristics (append closing brace / strip trailing commas) mask the signal and hide magnitude. We should not deploy masking broadly.
deploy-bot: Deployed peregrine-int4-canary -> infra/canary (rev r2026-int4-7) at 2026-03-21T18:03:10Z
ops-bot: Noted. Allocated small dedicated canary pool for experiments.
alex: Proposed immediate triage: 1) Run a short A/B canary: A) add explicit NDJSON sentinel delimiter between responses (e.g. "\\n--RDW-END--\\n") in the envelope only for canary clients, B) add per-fragment request_nonce header to detect cross-request merges, C) tightening the retry backoff to avoid overlapping streaming retries. 2) Collect full raw-fragment logs (hashed payload) + batch metadata.
priya: I can put together the envelope-sentinel A variant and a logging post-process that flags any fragments missing the sentinel. We'll keep it only in canary and behind a feature flag.
tan: Long-term fix might be ensuring the streaming layer emits a safe delimiter automatically or adding an actuator that zeroes decoder state between micro-batch slots for short sequences. Both require runtime work and perf validation.
qa-liz: I'll run a 10k-call canary for each variant (sentinel vs nonce vs control) over 4h windows and capture: parse_ok, fragment_count, last_token_hex, batch_size, retry_count. Can we run windows starting 2026-03-22T04:00Z?
alex: Yep. ops-bot, can you reserve time and attach trace hooks to capture the last 512 bytes of each stream event and the request_nonce when present?
ops-bot: Reserved. Tracing hooks added for 2026-03-22T04:00Z - 2026-03-22T12:00Z (staggered).
priya: Quick local numbers before full canary: control int4 w/ batching -> parse fail ~1.1%; int4 + sentinel -> down to ~0.05% (mostly detection, not fix). float16 control ~0.02%. Hits the same pattern as other quantized models.
tan: Good to validate sentinel doesn't change model output distribution. Also ensure backward compatibility: the sentinel will be in the envelope metadata not the generated text.
qa-liz: We'll only enable text-envelope sentinel in the canary header; no public clients are affected. Post-process will emit alerts for any rescued JSON while we run.
alex: OK plan set. We'll reconvene after canary results. If sentinel exposes huge cross-request merges we'll prioritize guardrails in the streaming transport. Thanks all.
